report.summary: Parsed personas.py chunk 1/1. Three public functions, one private helper. Docstring claims mostly uncheckable.
risks: _REGISTRY_PATH | low | Uses personas.json sibling file; missing file causes crash on first call. | Confirm personas.json exists and is valid JSON.
persona_for | medium | Default fallback returns provider name as persona, may be confusing. | Verify if this fallback is acceptable in design.
roster | low | Deduplication via dict.fromkeys preserves insertion order but may lose original order from pool. | Check if order matters.

claims.text: Each Claude specialist keeps its name on the trusted Claude lane, but gets a named *shadow* when the same role runs on a cheaper backend: a Chinese name on DeepSeek (external) and a Mexican/Italian name on local Ollama.
claims.why: The actual mapping (Claude, DeepSeek, Ollama) is in personas.json, not in this file. Cannot verify naming conventions.

claims.text: Purely cosmetic identity so reports and the architecture map read consistently.
claims.why: Purpose claim; no code in this chunk enforces or verifies cosmetic usage.

claims.text: Return the shadow persona's call-name for (provider, role).
claims.why: Function returns by_role.get(agent_name, prov.get('default', provider)), which is the call-name.

claims.text: All named workers on a lane: the per-role shadows plus any extra pool.
claims.why: Function returns list of by_role values plus pool, deduplicated.

observations.what: Module docstring describes a design where Claude specialists keep their name, but DeepSeek and Ollama get shadow names. This intent is not verifiable from this file alone.
_REGISTRY_PATH is a Path object constructed from __file__, assumes personas.json exists. No error handling for missing file or invalid JSON.
persona_for uses _registry() which is cached; if personas.json changes, cache persists until process restart.
roster deduplicates with dict.fromkeys; order preserves first occurrence of each name. If pool contains duplicates, they are removed.
